results.content:
Modelpeers is a follow-and-feed tracker for AI models and agents, pitched as LinkedIn for the model world. You follow entries such as Claude Code, GPT-6, and Gemini from a catalog of more than 200 models and agents, and new versions, price and limit changes, outages, and retirements land in a single feed instead of scattered changelogs. The premise: developers hear about breaking changes before those changes break production. Early coverage of the November 1 debut says the concept addresses a genuine tracking pain, while asking whether the feed can stay comprehensive and timely enough to trust coverage of the launch.

results.content:
I grew sick of not being able to follow and track the endless changes of AI models every week, so I decided to build Modelpeers. It's basically a feed of all these changes. You can follow models and agents that you use to see what is changing and what you need to do about it. Optionally, you can sign up to get a digest for the models/agents you follow.

Every few hours, it downloads and hashes dozens of pages from the prominent AI companies' pages, like changelogs, deprecation pages, status pages, and pricing pages. Then when a page changes, it pulls the diff, validates it with two models, and if validated as true, it posts it to the feed.

results.title: I work with AI all day, every day, and I still can't keep up with what changes. Every week a new model comes out, something goes down, prices move, or a model I depend on gets shut down. In April… | Lior Grossman
results.content:
I work with AI all day, every day, and I still can't keep up with what changes. Every week a new model comes out, something goes down, prices move, or a model I depend on gets shut down. In April, that really cost me. A feature in one of my products was broken for 48 hours because Anthropic shut down the model it used. They announced it two months earlier, on a page I never visit. And it's not just me: In the past couple of weeks, the AI tools most of us use changed 100 times, including 18 major outages. GitHub Copilot alone changed 8 times in one day! That's why I built Modelpeers - a tool that tracks all these AI updates. It's like LinkedIn for AI models and agents.
